title: When the Skylight Leak Is the Flashing
description: A skylight leak on a Houston roof is often the curb flashing, not a cracked dome. Putting new glass in the same hole does not stop the water.
html:
The ceiling ring under a skylight gets blamed on the glass. Sometimes the dome is cracked or the insulated glass has failed, and you can see it. More often the glass is fine and the metal around the curb is not. Replacing the skylight without redoing that metal puts a new unit in the same hole.

Curb, deck, and the kit

A curb-mounted skylight sits on a framed box. The flashing has to lap the shingles below, step up the sides, and slide under the shingles above, the same logic as a chimney, on a smaller scale. A deck-mounted unit uses a flange that weaves into the courses. Both fail when someone sets the unit in a bed of sealant and calls the sealant the flashing. Sealant is a gasket. It is not the water path.

From the attic, a leak at the uphill side of the curb means water is getting under the head flashing. A leak at a corner means a step is short or the underlayment was cut and never patched. Condensation is the lookalike: fog inside a failed pane, or drips on a cold morning with no rain. We do not sell a roof repair for a sealed unit that has lost its gas. We also do not sell a new skylight for a flashing problem.

What we do on a service call

We look at the curb wood, because a long leak rots the box and the deck around it. If the wood is sound and the flashing is the miss, that is a roof repair: new metal, woven back into the shingles, with the unit staying if it still seals. If the unit is yellowed, cracked, or weeping between the panes, we replace it and flash the new one. Doing only half is how the stain comes back.

Tell us whether the drip shows up in rain or on clear cold mornings. That one detail splits the job. Request a free inspection or call (281) 541-0027.
